scenes.heading: Vocabulary in context
scenes.sub: Unlock a word's meaning from the words around it
scenes.say: You don't need to know every word in the dictionary. In the reading test, the words around a tricky word will tell you what it means, if you know how to look.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: The shape of a jigsaw gap shows which piece fits
scenes.science: The words around a word show what it means
scenes.breaks: a jigsaw gap fits only one piece; in a sentence, several words might fit, so test every option.
scenes.say: Think of a jigsaw puzzle. You can tell which piece fits from the shape of the gap. A sentence works the same way. But sometimes more than one word seems to fit, so you test every option.

scenes.heading: Cover, predict, swap
steps: Read the sentence before and after
scenes.say: Here's the method. Read the sentence, and the ones around it. Cover the word. Predict a simple word that could go there. Then swap each option into the sentence and see which one keeps the meaning.

scenes.heading: Five context clues
points: Example: such as, like, a list
scenes.say: Look for five kinds of clue. A definition, often after a dash. A synonym nearby. A contrast, after words like but or unlike. Examples, after such as. Or the general sense of the whole situation.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: 'Although the first speaker was concise, the second rambled on for nearly an hour.' Concise means?
lines: Answer: brief and to the point
scenes.say: Although the first speaker was concise, the second rambled on for nearly an hour. Although is a contrast clue. The second speaker was long and rambling, so the first was the opposite: brief and to the point.

scenes.heading: Watch for the trap meaning

right.title: Meaning in the sentence
points: Draw a conclusion: work it out

scenes.say: Be careful with short, familiar words. The meaning you know best is often the trap. A team's spirits flagging means they grew weaker. Weathering a storm means surviving it.

Quick recap. Cover the word, predict, then swap each option in. Find the clue: definition, synonym, contrast, example or general sense. Check for surprise meanings, and don't take figures of speech literally. Now try the practice questions!
